title: The normalization of a scheme in a finite extension of a residue field is a normal integral scheme, integral over the base, with the extension as generic point
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $x\in X$ a point with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], $K/\kappa(x)$ a finite field extension, and $h:\operatorname{Spec}K	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)	o X$ the composite of the induced morphism with the canonical morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and there are a scheme $Y$, an integral morphism $
u:Y	o X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and a morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}K	o Y$ with $h=
u\circ g$ such that: (a) $Y$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] all of whose local rings $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ are integrally closed domains (Y is normal); (b) $g$ maps the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to the generic point $\eta_Y$ of $Y$ and induces an isomorphism $\kappa(\eta_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of fields, i.e. $g$ is the inclusion of the generic point of $Y$ with $K$ as function field. (One may take for $
u$ the normalization of $X$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, Stacks 035H: $Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal O')$ with $\mathcal O'$ the integral closure of $\mathcal O_X$ in $h_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$; if $Z\subseteq X$ is the reduced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{x\}}$, it is also the normalization of $Z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, by the last clause of Stacks 035I, which is the scheme used in the proof of Stacks 09Z6.)

Y is a normal integral scheme ... it is clear that K is the function field of Y'; the function-field identification is called clear there)

proof.text: Let h be the canonical composite Spec K -> X. Spec K is affine, hence compact and quasi-separated. Since X is quasi-separated, quasiCompact_of_compactSpace and QuasiSeparated.of_quasiSeparatedSpace give the two required morphism properties.

Take Y = h.normalization, nu = h.fromNormalization and g = h.toNormalization. The relative-normalization instances give IsIntegralHom nu and IsIntegral Y, and toNormalization_fromNormalization gives h = g >> nu.

The unique source stalk is isomorphic to K by stalkClosedPointIso and is integrally closed. Apply Scheme.Hom.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_normalization to h. The domain property of each stalk of Y follows from IsIntegral Y.

Dominance of g gives closure(range g) = Y. Since Spec K has one point xi, range g = {g(xi)}; thus g(xi) is generic. IsGenericPoint.eq identifies it with genericPoint Y, whose stalk is a field by Scheme.functionField. No existence theorem beyond the existing scheme generic-point API is needed.

Choose an affine open U containing h(xi)=x and identify sections on h^{-1}(U)=Spec K with K by theta. The proved private helper finite_residue_extension_integral_quotients identifies h.app U >> theta.hom with the germ at x followed by the residue map and the extension map, using germ_stalkClosedPointTo and germ_stalkClosedPointTo_Spec_fromSpecStalk. Give the stalk and K the compatible algebra structures. The finite field extension is integral; the residue map is surjective, hence integral, so every l in K is integral over the stalk by isIntegral_trans. IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk and IsIntegral.exists_multiple_integral_of_isLocalization produce b outside the affine prime such that b*l is integral over Gamma(X,U). The image of b is a unit in the stalk, and therefore has nonzero image in K by IsLocalization.map_units and IsUnit.map. Both b*l and b are integral over Gamma(X,U), and (b*l)/b=l. This directly proves the quotient calculation, without identifying A/p or invoking a separate fraction-field theorem.

Put psi=stalkClosedPointTo g. For any m integral over Gamma(X,U), theta.inv m is integral in the source sections by IsIntegral.map_of_comp_eq. Apply normalizationObjIso.inv to this integral element to obtain a section s of Y above U. The equality normalizationObjIso_hom_val, followed by germ_stalkClosedPointTo g, shows psi(germ(s))=m. Thus every integral numerator and denominator from the previous step is in the image of psi. The source of psi is a field, so psi preserves division; this proves surjectivity, and field-map injectivity gives bijectivity. Passing through the surjective residue map gives an isomorphism delta from the residue field of Y at g(xi) to K. The analogous descended map delta0 from the residue field of Spec K to K is an isomorphism using stalkClosedPointIso. The equalities residue_residueFieldMap and residue_descResidueField, cancelled against the epimorphic residue map of Y, show g.residueFieldMap xi >> delta0 = delta. IsIso.of_isIso_comp_right now gives the required residue-field isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem normalization_in_finite_residue_field_extension (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (x : X) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (X.residueField x) K] [Module.Finite (X.residueField x) K] : QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x) ∧ QuasiSeparated (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x) ∧ ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (ν : Y ⟶ X) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Y), IsIntegralHom ν ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x = g ≫ ν ∧ IsIntegral Y ∧ (∀ y : Y, IsDomain (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧ ∃ η : Y, IsGenericPoint η Set.univ ∧ g (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = η ∧ IsIso (g.residueFieldMap (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K))
